timeline.event: Mungo Man is buried beside Lake Mungo in western New South Wales
timeline.label: c. 40,000 years ago

timeline.event: Willem Janszoon makes the first recorded European landing
Dirk Hartog leaves an inscribed plate on the west coast
Abel Tasman reaches Van Diemen's Land
James Cook charts the east coast aboard HMS Endeavour
The First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove
Matthew Flinders completes his voyage around the continent
The Rum Rebellion overthrows Governor William Bligh
Gold rushes begin in New South Wales and Victoria
Gold miners clash with troops at the Eureka Stockade
Ned Kelly is captured after the siege at Glenrowan
The six colonies federate as the Commonwealth of Australia
Anzac troops land at Gallipoli
The Sydney Harbour Bridge opens
Gurindji workers walk off Wave Hill cattle station

places.name: Sydney Opera House
places.clue: Jørn Utzon's sail-roofed performing arts centre on Bennelong Point opened in 1973.

places.name: Uluru
places.clue: A sandstone monolith sacred to the Anangu people, rising about 348 m above the surrounding desert.

places.name: Canberra
places.clue: The purpose-built capital, designed by Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin around a central lake.

places.name: Melbourne
places.clue: Seat of the federal Parliament from Federation until 1927, and home of the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

places.name: Great Barrier Reef
places.clue: The world's largest coral reef system stretches about 2,300 km along the Queensland coast.

places.name: Perth
places.clue: Western Australia's capital on the Swan River, often called one of the world's most isolated big cities.

places.name: Kakadu National Park
places.clue: A World Heritage park of wetlands and escarpments with Aboriginal rock art, jointly managed with its traditional owners.

places.name: Twelve Apostles
places.clue: Limestone stacks carved by the Southern Ocean beside the Great Ocean Road; there were never twelve.

places.name: Port Arthur
places.clue: A former convict settlement on Tasmania's Tasman Peninsula, part of the Australian Convict Sites World Heritage listing.

places.name: Lake Mungo
places.clue: A dry lake bed where the remains of Mungo Lady and Mungo Man, buried around 40,000 years ago, were found.

places.name: Purnululu (Bungle Bungle Range)
places.clue: Orange-and-black striped sandstone domes shaped like beehives rise from the Kimberley plains here.

places.name: Coober Pedy
places.clue: An outback opal-mining town where many residents escape the heat by living in underground homes called dugouts.
